A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 43-page versions of the same work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-F without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original quantization experiments on Qwen3 and Llama, quantization-order analysis in Appendix D.3, and GPU inference measurements in Figures 4-5.

after.justification: v4 retains the original quantization results, quantization-order analysis, and GPU inference measurements reported in Section 5 and Appendices D-E.

M1.justification: The GPTQ/Babai procedures, min-pivot ordering, SSQR, HPTQ, and HRTN remain identical, including Algorithms 1-12 and the appendix pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both retain FineWeb-Edu calibration, WikiText-2/C4 perplexity evaluation, and the same zero-shot benchmarks on Qwen3 and Llama. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within every corresponding experiment. This includes RTN, GPTQ, HRTN and full-precision references, plus the AQLM, QuIP#, and QTIP comparison rows in Table 16.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings are identical, including 256 calibration sequences of 2048 tokens, act-order, group size 128 where specified, bitwidths, metrics, model configurations, and inference testing procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 retains the same quantization-order and error-bound analysis. The bitwidth, outlier-rate, model-scale, and batch-size analyses in Figures 4-5 and Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both specify 100-run averaging for random quantization order in Appendix D.3 and fixed-seed calibration in E.2. No run-count, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings match. For example, Table 3 reports identical 3.125-bit Qwen3-8B WikiText-2 perplexities: 10.34 for HPTQ and 12.77 for GPTQ.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, equivalence theorems, error bounds, and proofs in Sections 3-4 and Appendices B-D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about GPTQ-Babai equivalence, no-clipping error guarantees, quantizer accuracy, and efficient GPU kernels.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of min-pivot's modest accuracy benefits, overflow handling, and kernel performance. The no-clipping qualifications and proposed extensions to clipped grids and basis reduction are unchanged.

D1.justification: The source-code link, reproducibility statement, preprocessing instructions, implementation settings, and CUDA kernel details in Appendix E are identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the concurrent-work footnote retain identical citations and research positioning. No novelty claim or relationship to prior work changes.

P1.justification: Section 6 changes 'Future Work.' to 'Future work.' The arXiv margin stamp changes from v3 dated 2 Mar 2026 to v4 dated 13 May 2026. Otherwise, the wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-16 retain identical displays, captions, and placements. Page organization is unchanged; the localized stamp and capitalization edits do not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v4 only updates the arXiv stamp and the capitalization of 'Future work.' Scientific content, appendix proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and visual organization remain unchanged. These cosmetic edits produce no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
